video.title: Something's Happening to the Ozone Hole

protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Counterfactual: a massive hole over Antarctica; had we done nothing, a hole over the North Pole, over the whole planet by 2040, sunburn in five minutes. Hook is 'Directly over Antarctica ... was a massive hole' (the 22.6 line opens on 'it', and 45.2 opens on 'it' too). Payoff lands on 'That wasn't by accident. It was a choice.' (75.1); 'two choices ... for the better' (81.8) is an acceptable longer end.

Surprising facts about Antarctica: no one owns it, a treaty continent for peace and science; the sun never sets in summer; all time zones meet so there is none, and researchers pick the time zone of whoever feeds them. Hook 'No one owns Antarctica'; 208.9 ('Fewer than 5,000 people are allowed...') also works. Ends on 'their supply base,' before 'and to make things even more complicated' runs into the wind bit.

Story: in the 1950s Antarctica was almost a Cold War war zone of overlapping claims; geophysicists at a dinner party ask the superpowers to pause claiming land for 18 months to study it -- and it works. Hook 'If you time traveled back to the 1950s, this incredible place ... was almost a war zone.' Payoff 'this proposal actually works' (504.1); naming it the IGY (512.7) is acceptable.

Explanation: sea ice freezing around Antarctica pushes out salt that sinks and drives global currents -- currents in California, India, Australia are decided there, 'the heartbeat of the planet' -- and the continent is bigger than Europe or the US. Opens past 'You can see this if ... you flip it' (points back and at a map). Earliest landing is 'heartbeat of the planet' (555.8, ~24s, just under band); the size fact ending 'It's huge' (572.0) is preferred as in band. Both ends work.

Surprising fact: the ice averages over 2 km thick, holds ~91% of the world's fresh water, and melted would raise sea levels ~60 m -- 'All of this would be underwater. Well, there goes my home.' (the laugh is the payoff). Opens past 'They also learned...' (pronoun); 585.7 'Antarctica has a scary amount of water' is a tighter start (~23s).

Story of the fix: Dr. Solomon's team found an everyday chemical was destroying ozone; the world chose a different future; Solomon recalls being under the ozone hole in Antarctica when the Montreal Protocol was signed ('probably the last one to know'); every country signed, replacements were found, and 'it's working ... we're actually seeing the ozone layer recover' (784.9). Speakers inferred from text: Solomon speaks 738.4-757.8 and 772.7-780.4. Near the top of the band.

Closing take: you may think the Antarctic Treaty could never be signed today, but 'the current future is not the future future'; our grandparents signed the Treaty, our parents the Montreal Protocol -- are we going to be the generation that doesn't work together? Self-contained because it re-states both precedents. Ends 'we're going to do it again' (965.6) or 'not if we have anything to say about it' (961.1).

also_ok.why: Getting to Antarctica is sketchy: the Drake Passage (three oceans collide, ~800 shipwrecks) or a plane that lands on a runway made of ice. Travelogue, but the ice-runway line is a payoff.

Shorter cut of the fix: every country signed the Montreal Protocol, substitutes were found, and the ozone layer is recovering. Leans on 'those chemicals' from before the cut, so the longer clip is preferred.

negatives.why: Intro tease: 'you need to see this right now, because scientists say we need to make the next big choice' -- no payoff here.
Wind pushing her backward on the ice -- narration of what is on screen.
Solomon's team notices low ozone; 'what she was about to discover would forever change...' -- a tease whose answer comes six minutes later.
Snow blindness segues into the Mercury sponsor read.
Antarctic Treaty signed -- the payoff of the IGY story, but its setup ('they were figuring all of this out', the IGY) came minutes earlier.
Blue Rivers: 'this is unbelievably beautiful', drinking the meltwater -- on-screen moment, no standalone point.
